svg.title: How one question is run and scored
svg.desc: Six steps from left to right. History: the trimmed history, ten sessions fed one at a time with their dates. Write: the memory system turns each session into memory; the two baselines skip this step. Memory: what the system keeps. Read: at the question's date, the system picks what the answering model sees. Answer: the same model and LongMemEval's answer prompt for every system. Judge: LongMemEval's knowledge-update judge prompt answers yes or no. Three probes, each a model call, read the memory (is the new value stored, is the old one still there and still current), the context given to the answer (did the new value and the old one reach it), and the answer (did it give the old value).
svg.text: How one question is run and scored
The same six steps for every system. The judge gives the score; three probes say where a wrong answer was lost.
Is the new value in the memory? Is the
old one, and is it still presented as
Did the new value, and the old one, reach
Did the answer give the old value?
Each probe is a model call that reads text: the whole memory, the context given to the answer, or the answer. The old value is read once per
question from the first evidence session. For the baselines nothing is written, so only probes 2 and 3 apply.
